label: Starlark
notes: A session builds the whole engine (nothing shared between sessions), applies its limits, registers the host call function, then evaluates 1 + 1 and reads 2 back in Rust. Limits: Evaluator::set_max_callstack_size(100), set_max_heap_size(64MiB, best-effort), set_max_tick_count(1000000000) on every evaluator; Dialect::Standard (no while loops, no recursion); hermetic by design (no I/O builtins).
Memory: resident growth across 1,000 live sessions (stopped by target), measured first in a fresh process.

Tool call: the guest calls a registered Rust function on its own stack. Median of per-batch means, 1,000,000 calls in batches of 1,000 after 100,000 warm-ups; mean 0.1925 µs, slowest batch 0.3004 µs per call; 0.1925 µs of CPU per call.

Session = Globals (standard + our call module) + Module; an Evaluator is created per evaluation and is not kept. Modules only exist inside Module::with_temp_heap, so the memory phase nests sessions by recursion after pre-touching the stack it uses (memoryExtraStackBytes <= 0 means no stack was counted).
Host fn is a #[starlark_module] native fn(Value, Heap) -> Value; reply dict keys are static frozen strings.

starlark-rust only collects garbage between top-level module statements, never inside a function, so the tool-call module is one top-level `run(start, 1000)` statement per batch of 1,000 calls (same session, guest loop in the function body).

Secondary measurement, the whole loop as a single top-level statement (no GC until it returns; heap limit raised to 4GiB because garbage accumulates): toolCallWallUs=0.4107, toolCallCpuUs=0.4655 over 1000000 calls.
Compute: not measured in the Rust host.
